name: popover
purpose: Anchored, **non-modal** overlay that opens from a consumer-supplied trigger and renders rich, interactive content — a header (title + optional description + close), a free-form body, and a footer for actions — in a floating panel anchored to the trigger. Use for inline forms, filter builders, and contextual detail or confirmation that needs interactive children. Unlike `overlay/tooltip` (plain text, non-interactive) and `overlay/dialog` (modal, centered, focus-trapped), the popover leaves the page interactive, anchors to its trigger, and closes on `Esc` or outside-click. It differs from `navigation/dropdown`, which renders a menu of selectable options rather than free-form content.
useWhen: Interactive content anchored to a trigger while the page stays usable: an inline form, a filter builder, a quick edit of one field.
Contextual detail or a light confirmation that needs buttons or links inside it.
avoidWhen: A short, non-interactive hint on hover or focus → use `tooltip`.
A list of actions or options to pick from → use `dropdown`.
Choosing a form value from a list → use `select`.
A blocking task that must be completed or cancelled first → use `dialog`.
A long form or a secondary workflow → use `drawer`.
related: tooltip` — plain text only and non-interactive; opens on hover and focus, not on click.
dropdown` — same trigger and anchoring model, but renders option rows and emits `select`.
dialog` — modal and centered, traps focus and locks scroll; the popover does neither.
drawer` — edge-anchored modal panel for longer content.
bestPractices: Place `Popover.Trigger` first and `Popover.Content` after it. The trigger wires `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and the click toggle onto your element, so don't bind them yourself.
Include a `Popover.Title`. The panel takes its accessible name from it through `aria-labelledby`.
Set `width` for forms and filter builders so the panel doesn't resize as content changes. Without it, the panel sizes fluidly between the `--container-3xs` and `--container-xs` tokens.
Use `placement="auto"` for triggers that can sit near a viewport edge.
Set `dismissible` to `false` only when an outside click would discard input. Then give the user a way out: `Popover.Close` or a footer action.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Use with `v-model:open` or `@update:open`. When omitted, the component is uncontrolled.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the panel opens relative to the trigger. `'auto'` picks the best-fitting corner at open time based on available viewport space.

props.name: offset
props.doc: Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: width
props.doc: Panel width preset mapped to container tokens: `'small'` (`var(--container-xs)`), `'medium'` (`var(--container-sm)`), `'large'` (`var(--container-md)`). When omitted, the panel sizes fluidly between `var(--container-3xs)` and `var(--container-xs)`.

props.name: dismissible
props.doc: Light-dismiss: when `true`, the panel closes on outside-click and `Esc`. Set `false` to keep it open until the trigger or `PopoverClose` closes it.

events.name: update:open
events.notes: Fires on every open/closed transition; supports `v-model:open`. Emitted on trigger toggle, `Popover.Close`, `Esc`, and outside-click.
